display_title: 14-1-2 共享单车计划如何在世界各地发展

sentences.en: How Dutch engineer Luud Schimmelpennink helped to devise urban bike-sharing schemes
sentences.zh: 荷兰工程师卢德·席默尔彭宁克如何参与构思城市共享单车计划。

sentences.en: The original idea for an urban bike-sharing scheme dates back to a summer’s day in Amsterdam in 1965.
sentences.zh: 城市共享单车计划最初的构想，可以追溯到1965年阿姆斯特丹的一个夏日。

sentences.en: Provo, the organisation that came up with the idea, was a group of Dutch activists who wanted to change society.
sentences.zh: 提出这一构想的是普罗沃组织。它由一群希望改变社会的荷兰活动人士组成。

sentences.en: They believed the scheme, which was known as the Witte Fietsenplan, was an answer to the perceived threats of air pollution and consumerism.
sentences.zh: 他们把这个项目叫做“白色自行车计划”，认为它可以应对他们眼中空气污染和消费主义带来的威胁。

sentences.en: In the centre of Amsterdam, they painted a small number of used bikes white.
sentences.zh: 他们在阿姆斯特丹市中心把少量旧自行车漆成了白色。

sentences.en: They also distributed leaflets describing the dangers of cars and inviting people to use the white bikes.
sentences.zh: 他们还散发传单，说明汽车带来的危害，邀请人们骑这些白色自行车。

sentences.en: The bikes were then left unlocked at various locations around the city, to be used by anyone in need of transport.
sentences.zh: 接着，他们把自行车放在城内各处，不上锁，任何需要交通工具的人都能取用。

sentences.en: Luud Schimmelpennink, a Dutch industrial engineer who still lives and cycles in Amsterdam, was heavily involved in the original scheme.
sentences.zh: 荷兰工业工程师卢德·席默尔彭宁克至今仍在阿姆斯特丹生活和骑车。他当年深度参与了这项最早的计划。

sentences.en: He recalls how the scheme succeeded in attracting a great deal of attention — particularly when it came to publicising Provo’s aims — but struggled to get off the ground.
sentences.zh: 他回忆说，这个计划成功吸引了大量关注，尤其让更多人知道了普罗沃的宗旨，但要让计划真正运转起来却很难。

sentences.en: The police were opposed to Provo’s initiatives and almost as soon as the white bikes were distributed around the city, they removed them.
sentences.zh: 警方反对普罗沃的倡议。这些白色自行车刚分布到城内各处，警察几乎立刻就把车收走了。

sentences.en: However, for Schimmelpennink and for bike-sharing schemes in general, this was just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 然而，对席默尔彭宁克本人以及整个共享单车事业来说，这还只是个开端。

sentences.en: ‘The first Witte Fietsenplan was just a symbolic thing,’ he says.
sentences.zh: “最初的白色自行车计划只是个象征。”他说。

sentences.en: ‘We painted a few bikes white, that was all.
sentences.zh: “我们不过是把几辆自行车漆成白色，仅此而已。

sentences.en: Things got more serious when I became a member of the Amsterdam city council two years later.’
sentences.zh: 两年后，我成了阿姆斯特丹市议会议员，事情这才认真做了起来。”

sentences.en: Schimmelpennink seized this opportunity to present a more elaborate Witte Fietsenplan to the city council.
sentences.zh: 席默尔彭宁克抓住这个机会，向市议会提交了一份更为详尽的白色自行车计划。

sentences.en: ‘My idea was that the municipality of Amsterdam would distribute 10,000 white bikes over the city, for everyone to use,’ he explains.
sentences.zh: 他解释说：“我的想法是，由阿姆斯特丹市政府在全市投放一万辆白色自行车，供所有人使用。

sentences.en: ‘I made serious calculations.
sentences.zh: 我认真算过这笔账。

sentences.en: It turned out that a white bicycle — per person, per kilometre — would cost the municipality only 10% of what it contributed to public transport per person per kilometre.’
sentences.zh: 结果发现，按每人每公里计算，白色自行车给市政府带来的成本，只相当于市政府按相同标准为公共交通投入资金的10%。”

sentences.en: Nevertheless, the council unanimously rejected the plan.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，市议会还是一致否决了这个计划。

sentences.en: ‘They said that the bicycle belongs to the past.
sentences.zh: “他们说自行车属于过去。

sentences.en: They saw a glorious future for the car,’ says Schimmelpennink.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，汽车前途无量。”席默尔彭宁克说。

sentences.en: But he was not in the least discouraged.
sentences.zh: 可他丝毫没有气馁。

sentences.en: Schimmelpennink never stopped believing in bike-sharing, and in the mid-90s, two Danes asked for his help to set up a system in Copenhagen.
sentences.zh: 席默尔彭宁克始终相信共享单车行得通。20世纪90年代中期，两位丹麦人请他帮忙在哥本哈根建立一套系统。

sentences.en: The result was the world’s first large-scale bike-share programme.
sentences.zh: 于是，世界上第一个大规模共享单车项目诞生了。

sentences.en: It worked on a deposit: ‘You dropped a coin in the bike and when you returned it, you got your money back.’
sentences.zh: 它采用押金制：“你往自行车里投一枚硬币，还车时就能把钱取回来。”

sentences.en: After setting up the Danish system, Schimmelpennink decided to try his luck again in the Netherlands — and this time he succeeded in arousing the interest of the Dutch Ministry of Transport.
sentences.zh: 建成丹麦的系统后，席默尔彭宁克决定回荷兰再试一次。这次他成功引起了荷兰交通部的兴趣。

sentences.en: ‘Times had changed,’ he recalls.
sentences.zh: “时代已经变了。”他回忆说。

sentences.en: ‘People had become more environmentally conscious, and the Danish experiment had proved that bike-sharing was a real possibility.’
sentences.zh: “人们的环保意识增强了，而且丹麦的试验也证明，共享单车确实可行。”

sentences.en: A new Witte Fietsenplan was launched in 1999 in Amsterdam.
sentences.zh: 1999年，阿姆斯特丹推出了一项新的白色自行车计划。

sentences.en: However, riding a white bike was no longer free; it cost one guilder per trip and payment was made with a chip card developed by the Dutch bank Postbank.
sentences.zh: 不过，这次骑白色自行车不再免费，每骑一次要花一荷兰盾，车费通过荷兰邮政银行开发的芯片卡支付。

sentences.en: Schimmelpennink designed conspicuous, sturdy white bikes locked in special racks which could be opened with the chip card — the plan started with 250 bikes, distributed over five stations.
sentences.zh: 席默尔彭宁克设计的白色自行车醒目又结实，锁在专用车架上，刷芯片卡便能开锁。计划启动时共有250辆车，分布在五个站点。

sentences.en: Theo Molenaar, who was a system designer for the project, worked alongside Schimmelpennink.
sentences.zh: 特奥·莫勒纳尔是这个项目的系统设计师，和席默尔彭宁克共事。

sentences.en: ‘I remember when we were testing the bike racks, he announced that he had already designed better ones.
sentences.zh: “我记得，我们还在测试停车架时，他就宣布自己已经设计出了更好的。

sentences.en: But of course, we had to go through with the ones we had.’
sentences.zh: 可我们当然还是得用现有的车架把项目做下去。”

sentences.en: The system, however, was prone to vandalism and theft.
sentences.zh: 然而，这套系统很容易遭到蓄意破坏，车辆也很容易失窃。

sentences.en: ‘After every weekend there would always be a couple of bikes missing,’ Molenaar says.
sentences.zh: “每个周末一过，总会少上两三辆车。”莫勒纳尔说。

sentences.en: ‘I really have no idea what people did with them, because they could instantly be recognised as white bikes.’
sentences.zh: “我真不知道人们把车弄去干什么，因为一眼就能认出它们是白色自行车。”

sentences.en: But the biggest blow came when Postbank decided to abolish the chip card, because it wasn’t profitable.
sentences.zh: 但打击最大的是，邮政银行认为芯片卡无利可图，决定停用这种卡。

sentences.en: ‘That chip card was pivotal to the system,’ Molenaar says.
sentences.zh: “那张芯片卡是这套系统运作的关键。”莫勒纳尔说。

sentences.en: ‘To continue the project we would have needed to set up another system, but the business partner had lost interest.’
sentences.zh: “要继续开展这个项目，我们就得另建一套系统，但我们的商业伙伴已经失去了兴趣。”

sentences.en: Schimmelpennink was disappointed, but — characteristically — not for long.
sentences.zh: 席默尔彭宁克很失望，但按他一贯的性格，这种失望并没有持续多久。

sentences.en: In 2002 he got a call from the French advertising corporation JC Decaux, who wanted to set up his bike-sharing scheme in Vienna.
sentences.zh: 2002年，他接到法国广告公司德高集团的电话，对方想在维也纳推行他的共享单车方案。

sentences.en: ‘That went really well.
sentences.zh: “事情进展得非常顺利。

sentences.en: After Vienna, they set up a system in Lyon.
sentences.zh: 继维也纳之后，他们又在里昂建立了一套系统。

sentences.en: Then in 2007, Paris followed.
sentences.zh: 随后在2007年，巴黎也跟了上来。

sentences.en: That was a decisive moment in the history of bike-sharing.’
sentences.zh: 那是共享单车史上的一个决定性时刻。”

sentences.en: The huge and unexpected success of the Parisian bike-sharing programme, which now boasts more than 20,000 bicycles, inspired cities all over the world to set up their own schemes, all modelled on Schimmelpennink’s.
sentences.zh: 巴黎共享单车项目取得了出人意料的巨大成功，如今已有两万多辆自行车。这促使世界各地的城市纷纷推出自己的方案，都是以席默尔彭宁克的设计为蓝本。

sentences.en: ‘It’s wonderful that this happened,’ he says.
sentences.zh: “能有这样的结果，真是太好了。”他说。

sentences.en: ‘But financially I didn’t really benefit from it, because I never filed for a patent.’
sentences.zh: “不过在经济上，我其实没从中得到什么好处，因为我从来没有申请过专利。”

sentences.en: In Amsterdam today, 38% of all trips are made by bike and, along with Copenhagen, it is regarded as one of the two most cycle-friendly capitals in the world — but the city never got another Witte Fietsenplan.
sentences.zh: 如今，阿姆斯特丹38%的出行是骑自行车完成的。它和哥本哈根被视为世界上两个最适合骑行的首都，但阿姆斯特丹一直没有再推出白色自行车计划。

sentences.en: Molenaar believes this may be because everybody in Amsterdam already has a bike.
sentences.zh: 莫勒纳尔认为，这或许是因为阿姆斯特丹人已经人手一辆自行车。

sentences.en: Schimmelpennink, however, cannot see that this changes Amsterdam’s need for a bike-sharing scheme.
sentences.zh: 但席默尔彭宁克认为，这一点并没有改变阿姆斯特丹对共享单车计划的需要。

sentences.en: ‘People who travel on the underground don’t carry their bikes around.
sentences.zh: “乘地铁的人不会随身带着自己的自行车。

sentences.en: But often they need additional transport to reach their final destination.’
sentences.zh: 但他们下了地铁，常常还需要其他交通工具才能到达最终目的地。”

sentences.en: Although he thinks it is strange that a city like Amsterdam does not have a successful bike-sharing scheme, he is optimistic about the future.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，像阿姆斯特丹这样的城市竟然没有成功的共享单车方案，的确很奇怪，但他对未来很乐观。

sentences.en: ‘In the ‘60s we didn’t stand a chance because people were prepared to give their lives to keep cars in the city.
sentences.zh: “在20世纪60年代，我们没有丝毫胜算，因为人们宁可豁出性命也要让汽车留在城里。

sentences.en: But that mentality has totally changed.
sentences.zh: 然而，那种心态已经彻底变了。

sentences.en: Today everybody longs for cities that are not dominated by cars.’
sentences.zh: 如今，人人都盼望城市不再由汽车主宰。”

questions.question: a description of how people misused a bike-sharing scheme
an explanation of why a proposed bike-sharing scheme was turned down
a reference to a person being unable to profit from their work
an explanation of the potential savings a bike-sharing scheme would bring
a reference to the problems a bike-sharing scheme was intended to solve
Which TWO of the following statements are made in the text about the Amsterdam bike-sharing scheme of 1999?

options.A: It was initially opposed by a government department.
options.B: It failed when a partner in the scheme withdrew support.
options.C: It aimed to be more successful than the Copenhagen scheme.
options.D: It was made possible by a change in people's attitudes.
options.E: It attracted interest from a range of bike designers.

questions.logic: B 看项目为什么停。银行停用芯片卡，要延续项目就得另建系统，合作方却失去了兴趣。D 看项目为什么能启动。人们的环保意识增强，又有丹麦的成功先例，这解释了为什么同样的想法这次能得到响应。

questions.question: Which TWO of the following statements are made in the text about Amsterdam today?

options.A: The majority of residents would like to prevent all cars from entering the city.
options.B: There is little likelihood of the city having another bike-sharing scheme.
options.C: More trips in the city are made by bike than by any other form of transport.
options.D: A bike-sharing scheme would benefit residents who use public transport.
options.E: The city has a reputation as a place that welcomes cyclists.

questions.logic: D 对应地铁乘客的最后一段路。他们乘地铁时不带自行车，却常需要接驳交通，共享单车能补上这一段。E 对应阿姆斯特丹与哥本哈根并列为全球对骑行者最友好的两座首都之一，体现的是城市声誉。
